topic: The hidden geometry of A-series paper
centralQuestion: Why can A-series paper keep its proportions when halved?
thesis: A √2 aspect ratio makes the rotated half-sheet similar to its parent; physical sizes approximate the ideal.
viewerPayoff: Understand a familiar design and distinguish length scaling from area scaling.

claims.statement: A square bisected parallel to one side yields a rectangle whose long-to-short ratio is two, rather than one.

caveats.statement: Ideal models are exact; physical sheet dimensions are rounded and toleranced.
Scaling preserves proportions; it does not guarantee borderless printing or universal paper applicability.

hooks.text: Cut A4 paper in half. Turn it. It’s almost the same shape, only smaller.
hooks.viewerPromise: Watch the shape survive a cut and learn why.

hooks.text: Half the area does not mean half the length.
